text: Provide converters from docker-compose.yml and devcontainer.json to environment.yaml, reporting unsupported constructs explicitly.
rationale: Developers will not hand-rewrite dozens of project environments to try os env.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the dev environment implementation for services like Postgres (Linux personality OCI images, native packages, or both) after measuring the 50 ms cached startup target for each.
rationale: Most developer services exist only as Linux software, so the native environment story depends on this compatibility decision.

text: Cached build outputs from native development environments must be stored as content-addressed objects (cross-ref ENV).
History must record development environment changes (e.g. 'Changed project environment') (cross-ref ENV).
Restore must be able to revert workspaces (open projects, environments).
Implement development isolation as a native OS primitive (a DevelopmentEnvironment object composed from native primitives), not as a userspace tool layered on containers.
Do not require a Docker daemon for native development environments.
Do not require a Linux VM for native development environments.
Do not require an overlay filesystem stack for native development environments; use storage snapshots (§26) instead.
Do not require image extraction to start a development environment; map immutable package objects directly (§34).
Do not require Docker Desktop or any equivalent desktop VM manager for development environments.
Define and implement the environment.yaml project definition format with top-level runtime, services and resources sections.
Implement the environment.yaml runtime section (e.g. php: 8.6) resolving named runtime versions to immutable packages from the content-addressed store (§27, §29).
Implement the environment.yaml services section (e.g. postgres: 19, redis: 10) instantiating each service as an isolated Component with its own capabilities.
Implement the environment.yaml resources section (memory: 4GB, cpu: 4) mapping directly onto ResourceDomain budgets (§23).
Environment creation must create a ResourceDomain for the environment.
Environment creation must create a StorageSnapshot (copy-on-write view of project and dependency storage, §26).
Environment creation must create a CapabilityNamespace scoping which capabilities components inside the environment may hold.
Environment creation must create a NetworkNamespace isolating service ports and network policy for the environment.
Environment creation must instantiate the Components declared by runtime and services entries inside the environment's ResourceDomain and namespaces.
Implement an environment cache (pre-resolved packages, pre-created snapshots, warm component images) so the < 50 ms cached startup target is attainable.
Decide whether environment.yaml is a distinct schema or a profile of the package manifest (§28), and whether YAML or a typed manifest format is the canonical source (ADR).
Resolve how environment.yaml version specifiers (php: 8.6, postgres: 19) are locked, where the lock file lives, and how service packages are discovered in the package repository.
Resolve how the environment's NetworkNamespace exposes service endpoints (postgres, redis) to the developer's shell, IDE and browser without granting ambient network authority.
Record environment changes as system history events (§31 lists 'Changed project environment') so os history and os restore cover environments.

Development environments must be able to run Linux-personality runtimes and services (php, postgres, redis are Linux software) inside native isolation; document the dependency on LNX for environment components.
Environment definitions must be reproducible: identical environment.yaml plus lock must yield identical immutable component sets (§27, §29).
Build a reference environment.yaml demo (php + postgres + redis) that is used as the V1 acceptance test for dev environments.
Native software should rarely need containers; no native subsystem may depend on an OCI runtime.
Development environments via 'os env enter' from environment.yaml (cross-ref §35).
